Can you point us to the operational playbook and confirm whether we can stipulate custody routing to our vendor in the DPA? Attaching our redline DPA (short) and a high-level network diagram.

Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks and the redline. Short answers up front, details below:

- Yes, we support customer-directed escrow routing in constrained geos. We can add a DPA clause to allow Orchid to designate an approved escrow vendor; Redwood will coordinate key export and provide notarized handoff artifacts.
- Operator subprocessors: we have a limited set (listed below) for on-call/maintenance paths. We can provide a filtered telemetry report and minimize PII in all operator logs.
- Notice windows: we can commit to 48-hour notice for planned interventions. Emergency breakglass is defined in our runbook; event-level audit trails and signed breakglass justification will be available.

Detail: custody routing options
1) Two patterns we commonly use: (A) Custody-forward: upon initial provisioning Redwood performs a one-time key escrow export to the vendor Orchid designates, with both parties (vendor + Orchid) acknowledging via signed handoff. Redwood retains no copy after the export unless Orchid asks us to hold a sealed escrow under a customer-approved KMS model. (B) Escrow-proxy: Redwood holds an encrypted escrow protected by a split-key held by a neutral notary/escrow partner; the partner releases on mutually-agreed triggers.

Operational impacts:
- Pattern A requires a 4–8 business day coordination window for notarization; export artifacts include export manifest, signed certificate, and a KMS-wrap proof. We can template this process into the DPA’s Annex B.
- Pattern B preserves faster restore options but requires listing the escrow partner as a subprocessor.

Telemetry & subprocessors
- Subprocessors that may touch maintenance logs: OpsOnCall LLC (support engineers), InfraSight (GPU fleet diagnostics), and LogSafe (audit store).
- During operator breakglass we record session logs, command transcripts, and ephemeral telnet/ssh session transcripts where applicable. PII is redacted by default; we can provide a filtered artifacts bundle for audits.

Notice & breakglass
- Planned work: 48-hour notice, scheduled maintenance windows, and a rollback plan.
- Emergency breakglass: defined triggers (SLA-impacting incidents, catastrophic data-loss) with post-hoc justification within 24 hours and event artifacts (session logs, signed release form).

Next steps: I’ll loop Kim (legal) and Irene (privdep ops) to draft the DPA language and an Annex for the custody routing diagram. Can we set a 30-min call Monday to lock scope?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Alex / team —

I reviewed Sean’s operational notes and Orchid's redline. A few legal/contractual clarifications:

1) If Orchid designates a third-party escrow vendor (Pattern A), we need the vendor’s contract/scope to include: breach notification commitments, limited audit rights, and an explicit non-use clause (no access to customer workloads). Without that we will not accept a silent escrow.

2) Listing subprocessors: we will add a schedule listing OpsOnCall LLC et al. but propose a 30-day notification for new subprocessors, and a customer objection window for critical subprocessors (per DPA standard).

3) Jurisdictional export: custody export artifacts may contain metadata that triggers data export controls — we propose a clause allowing Orchid to require an EU-only escrow path if the workload is EU-personal-data-processed. That will affect execution timelines.

Irene, please draft a short Annex with the handshake states (provision -> export -> acknowledgement -> certificate issuance) and include retention periods for export manifests. Alex/Maya, if you can provide the escrow vendor details (name, contact, contract window) we can bolt these into Annex B and a DocuSign-ready DPA.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Operational notes to supplement Kimberly and Sean:

- Timeline: For Pattern A (customer-directed escrow export) ops needs a 6 business day lead to schedule notarization, KMS wrap, and a secure courier (if hardware tokens involved). If Orchid wants an EU-only path we need an additional compliance check (2–3 business days).
- Technical controls: we will create a hashed export manifest (SHA256) and publish the manifest to a signed S3 object for Orchid + escrow vendor access. Redwood will retain the manifest for 24 months for audit only; keys are not stored unwrapped.
- Breakglass steps: 1) Issue incident ticket -> 2) Ops triage -> 3) Exec approval for breakglass -> 4) Justification and session recording turned on -> 5) Remediate -> 6) Post-mortem artifact bundle sent to customer.

I’ll attach an ops-ready Annex (text) to the redline. Sean — please confirm the 30-min call and I’ll bring the runbook snippet.
